3 clean dataset and remove duplicates/suffixed

Keep .x versions from RdRP table, not .y from contig table.

rdrp_clean <- rdrp_contigs |> 
  select(
    Full_name,
    RID = RID.x,
    ND = ND.x,
    Treatment,
    Site, Subplot, Layer,
    Order = Order.x,
    Family = Family.x,
    Genus = Genus.x,
    Phylum = Phylum.x,
    Novel = Novel.x,
    Segmented = Segmented.x,
    Length = Length.x,
    Host = Host.x,
    Host_Evidence = Host_Evidence.x,
    Contig,
    `Contig length`
  ) |> 
  distinct()

Every ND treatment shpws genome richness= 1 expected because each RDRP hit maps to one contig so each ND record contributes one unique contig in the joined table.

1 Calulating VOTUs

create using RvANI90 (Average nucleotide identity at a 90 percent threshold Used to cluster contigs into species-like viral OTUs.) and RCR90 (Reciprocal coverage ratio Ensures contigs belong to the same genome / species)

RVMT’s rule: Contigs belong to the same VOTU if RvANI90 ≥ 90% AND RCR90 ≥ 90%. These metrics are calculated, need to be converted into cluster IDs

viral <- read_tsv(
  "/work/pi_jlb_umass_edu/blanchardlab/RVMT_Zenodo_V4/RVMT_Zenodo_V4/Expanded_Contig_Set/viral_contigs_annotated_full.tsv"
)

7 identify treatment-specific VOTUs (anything in both is ignored)

genomes_per_votu_treat <- votu_rdrp |>
  group_by(Treatment, VOTU) |>
  summarize(GenomeCount = n_distinct(Contig), .groups = "drop")


votu_matrix <- genomes_per_votu_treat |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = Treatment,
    values_from = GenomeCount,
    values_fill = 0
  )

Present in heated but absent in control

heated_only_count <- votu_matrix |>
  filter(C == 0 & H > 0) |>
  nrow()

heated_only_count

888 VOTUs exclusive to heated soils

Present in controls but absent in heated

control_only_count <- votu_matrix |>
  filter(H == 0 & C > 0) |>
  nrow()

control_only_count
[1] 1738

1738 VOTUs exclusive to control soils

Genome counts by treatment, reshape into long format for plotting and then plot counts per VOTU

votu_matrix <- genomes_per_votu_treat |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = Treatment,
    values_from = GenomeCount,
    values_fill = 0
  )
votu_long <- votu_matrix |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(C, H), 
               names_to = "Treatment", 
               values_to = "GenomeCount")
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(votu_long, aes(x = Treatment, y = GenomeCount, fill = Treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Genome Counts per VOTU in Heated vs Control Soils",
    x = "",
    y = "Genome Count"
  )
ggplot(votu_long, aes(x = Treatment, y = GenomeCount, fill = Treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 10)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Genome Counts per VOTU (0–10)",
    x = "",
    y = "Genome Count"
  )
# 1-5 zoom 
ggplot(votu_long, aes(x = Treatment, y = GenomeCount, fill = Treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 5)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Genome Counts per VOTU (Zoomed: 0–5)",
    x = "",
    y = "Genome Count"
  )

What this could mean :

Most VOTUs in both treatments have GenomeCount= 1. Most RNA virus “species” assemble into 1 contig.

Control VOTUs have more contigs per species.

Heated have far fewer extreme outliers highlighted in the 1-10 ??… Heated have no large clusters and Control has a small populaiton of complex VOTUs

# adding taxonomy to VOTUs 
votu_taxonomy <- votu_rdrp |>
  group_by(VOTU, Treatment) |>
  summarize(
    Orders = paste(unique(Order), collapse = "; "),
    Families = paste(unique(Family), collapse = "; "),
    Genera = paste(unique(Genus), collapse = "; "),
    GenomeCount = n_distinct(Contig),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

Genome count distribution faceted by phylum

ggplot(votu_taxonomy2, aes(x = GenomeCount, fill = Treatment)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = 0.6, position = "identity") +
  facet_wrap(~ Phylum, scales = "free_y") +

Chi test do h v c differ in inflation structure?

tbl <- table(votu_taxonomy2$Treatment, votu_taxonomy2$GC_bin)
chisq.test(tbl)

    Pearson's Chi-squared test

data:  tbl
X-squared = 14.349, df = 3, p-value = 0.002467

pvalue of .002467. Highly significant. H vC do not produce VOTUS of the sane fragemntation

compare means/medians for typical genome count between treatments

wilcox.test(GenomeCount ~ Treatment, data = votu_taxonomy2)

    Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction

data:  GenomeCount by Treatment
W = 1253972, p-value = 0.002714
alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0

This could tell us that the typical genome assmebles differently under warming, heating reduces fragmentaiton (collapsing community) or increases highly framented VOTUs.

tail probalilties

tbl_tail <- table(
  votu_taxonomy2$Treatment,
  votu_taxonomy2$GenomeCount > 5
)

chisq.test(tbl_tail)

    Pearson's Chi-squared test with Yates' continuity correction

data:  tbl_tail
X-squared = 9.4906, df = 1, p-value = 0.002065

Probanlity of a VOTU having fragmentation >5 is significantly different between treatments

Alluvial flow digram frgament flows

library(ggalluvial)

alluvial_df <- votu_taxonomy2 |>
  mutate(
    GC_bin = case_when(
      GenomeCount <= 1 ~ "1",
      GenomeCount <= 3 ~ "2–3",
      GenomeCount <= 6 ~ "4–6",
      TRUE ~ ">6"
    )
  )

ggplot(alluvial_df,
       aes(axis1 = Treatment, axis2 = GC_bin)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = GC_bin), width = 1/12) +
  geom_stratum(width = 1/12, fill = "grey90") +
  geom_label(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum))) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Flow of VOTU Fragmentation Categories Between Treatments")

Thicker bands.. more VOTUs. Control has more VOTUS overall (2000ish) You can see wider ribbons flow into bins from control that have more fragments

cleaner version of flow

flow_df <- alluvial_df |>
  count(Treatment, GC_bin, name = "Freq")

ggplot(flow_df,
  aes(axis1 = Treatment, axis2 = GC_bin, y = Freq)) +

  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = GC_bin),
    width = 0.25, alpha = 0.6, knot.pos = 0.4) +

  geom_stratum(width = 0.25, fill = "grey95", color = "black") +

  geom_label(
    stat = "stratum",
    aes(label = paste0(after_stat(stratum),
                       "\n",
                       round(after_stat(prop)*100,1), "%")),
    fill = "white", size = 4
  ) +

  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Treatment","Fragmentation Bin"),
                   expand = c(.05,.05)) +

  scale_fill_manual(values=c(
    "1"="#A6D854","2–3"="#66C2A5",
    "4–6"="#8DA0CB",">6"="#FC8D62")) +

  labs(title="Flow of VOTU Fragmentation Categories",
       y="Number of VOTUs", x="", fill="Genome Count Bin") +

  theme_minimal(base_size=15)+
  theme(axis.text.y=element_blank(),
        panel.grid=element_blank())

Limitation of the package is ribbons cant be labeled directly, only stratum labels

Which phyla controbute msot to heated only vs control only VOTUS

# create heated-only, control-only, shared
votu_status <- votu_matrix |>
  mutate(
    Status = case_when(
      C > 0 & H > 0 ~ "Shared",
      C > 0 & H == 0 ~ "Control-only",
      H > 0 & C == 0 ~ "Heated-only"
    )
  )

# bring taxonomy
votu_status_tax <- votu_status |>
  left_join(votu_taxonomy2, by = "VOTU")

# plot phylum composition for only heated-only VOTUs

  filter(Status == "Heated-only") |>
  count(Phylum)
